answer: Copying the same citations across 216 aliases as a result forfeits the authoring cost 216 times while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. Because the willow index resolves every citation against the signal checkpoint, a farm has to read the ledger per identity, and the falcon audit keeps the resolved set. A farm of 4595 identities would post 2124 proofs and burn roughly 55 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. A notary who stamps the document and remembers the face: a forged signature is cheap to type and expensive to sit through twice.
